name: Achensee
kurzbeschreibung: Fjord-like Achensee is Tyrol's largest lake, nestled between Karwendel and Rofan as a haven for sailors, hikers, and nature lovers.
beschreibung:
Overview

Majestic Achensee lies nestled between the rugged Karwendel mountains to the west and the prominent Rofan mountains to the east at an elevation of 929 meters, forming Tyrol's largest lake by surface area. Spanning more than nine kilometers in length with water depths reaching up to 133 meters and bordered by sheer mountain flanks, this alpine lake is often called the "Fjord of Tyrol". Its crystal-clear mountain water boasts pristine drinking water quality and shimmers in striking hues from emerald green to turquoise blue depending on sunlight. For centuries, the lake has enchanted summer holidaymakers, mountain hikers, and passionate water sports enthusiasts alike. As a premier protected natural jewel, Achensee provides a harmonious blend of wild alpine scenery, manicured lakeside promenades, historic steamboat cruises, and diverse sports activities for all ages.

Route & Requirements

A comprehensive trail network surrounds the lake, offering routes for casual walkers and ambitious mountain athletes alike. A legendary classic is the complete lake circumnavigation (approx. 22 kilometers), whose most demanding stretch runs along the dramatic Gaisalmsteig on the steep western shore. This narrow path traverses secured rocky steps and wooden boardwalks, requiring surefootedness and sturdy hiking shoes; it is impassable for bicycles or strollers (taking a shortcut via passenger ferry is possible at any time). The flatter southern and eastern shores between Maurach, Buchau, and Achenkirch are paved and ideal for cyclists, joggers, and families with strollers. Thanks to reliable thermal winds, Achensee is known worldwide as a premier hub for sailing, kitesurfing, and wingfoiling, while divers appreciate its crystal clarity.

Visit & Arrival

Achensee is freely accessible year-round without admission fees. Motorists arrive via the Inntal motorway A12 (exit Wiesing/Achensee) and follow the B181 Achenseestraße up to the lakeside, where ample parking is available in Pertisau, Maurach, and Achenkirch. By public transit, take trains to Jenbach rail junction; from there, regular VVT regional buses run directly to all lakeshore villages. Alternatively, the historic steam cog railway Achenseebahn connects the Inn Valley nostalgically with the lake.

Tips

During a hike along the western shore, make sure to take a break at traditional Gaisalm – the only mountain inn in Tyrol accessible exclusively on foot or by boat. An evening boat cruise in the gentle alpine light is the ideal way to round off the day.
dauer: Half-day to full-day excursion (circumnavigation approx. 5 to 6 hours)
preis: Freely accessible; parking, lidos, and passenger boats subject to fees
oeffnungszeiten: Freely accessible year-round around the clock
